plain.text: The serpent was more crafty than any other animal. It asked the woman, "Did God really say, 'You must not eat from any tree in the garden'?" She said they could eat from the trees, except the one in the middle; if they ate from it or touched it they would die. "You will not surely die," said the serpent. "God knows that when you eat it your eyes will be opened and you will be like God, knowing good and evil." The woman saw that the fruit looked good and desirable for gaining wisdom. She ate some and gave some to her husband, who was with her, and he ate it. Then their eyes were opened and they realised they were naked, so they sewed fig leaves together to cover themselves.

They heard the LORD God walking in the garden in the cool of the day, and they hid among the trees. God called, "Where are you?" The man said, "I heard you in the garden, and I was afraid because I was naked, so I hid." God asked if he had eaten from the forbidden tree. The man blamed the woman, "whom you gave to be with me". The woman said, "The serpent deceived me, and I ate."

God cursed the serpent above all animals: it would crawl on its belly and eat dust. "I will put hostility between you and the woman, and between your offspring and hers. He will crush your head, and you will strike his heel."

To the woman God said she would have great pain in childbirth, and that she would desire her husband, and he would rule over her. To the man he said that because he listened to his wife and ate from the tree, the ground was cursed; he would have to work hard all his life to get food from it, among thorns and thistles. "For dust you are, and to dust you shall return." The man named his wife Eve, because she would be the mother of all the living.

The LORD God made garments of skin and clothed them. God said that the man had become like one of us, knowing good and evil, and must not also eat from the tree of life and live forever. So God sent him out of the garden of Eden to work the ground. He placed cherubim and a flaming sword east of the garden to guard the way to the tree of life.

summary.bigIdea: The first people doubt God's word and disobey, bringing shame, blame, pain and death, yet God still cares for them.
points: The serpent makes the woman doubt God's goodness.
After eating, they hide in shame and blame each other.
There are painful consequences, but God clothes them and promises the serpent will one day be crushed.
summary.reflection: God called out, "Where are you?" If God asked you that today, how would you answer?
